actor_as_reported: Alexandroni Brigade / emerging Israeli forces (agency attribution provisional)
event_categories: occupation; alleged executions of captives; detention; depopulation
affected_people_or_estimate: Palestinian villagers; count of killings unresolved
evidence_summary: Later survivor testimony and Israeli veteran testimony are reported; forensic spatial analysis identifies possible mass-grave sites; no exhumation or court finding in sources reviewed
evidence_status: Contested allegation with corroborating testimony and spatial evidence; denial and disagreement preserved
legal_status: No judicial finding; legal classification unadjudicated
scope_decision: Include as a sourced allegation; do not enter an exact death toll
limitations: Guardian reports estimates of 40–200, which are not a verified count. Forensic Architecture maps possible grave sites; the site was not excavated. Current scholarship differentiates village occupation/evacuation and alleged post-surrender killings. State-formation command chain on 22–23 May requires source-specific care.

actor_as_reported: Israeli Army and Palmach troops (as identified by contemporary press and later research)
event_categories: military capture; mass detention of men; expulsion of civilians
affected_people_or_estimate: Thousands of men reported captive; contemporary correspondent counted 3,000–4,000 at Lydda and about 1,500 at Ramle; later scholarship estimates 60,000–70,000 expelled
evidence_summary: Contemporary U.S. newspaper report filed from Lydda; UN Mediator's 1948 report says occupation of the towns and villages augmented refugee numbers; later scholarship reconstructs forced expulsion
evidence_status: Capture and mass detention contemporaneously reported; coercive expulsion documented by later historical research; individual death/displacement counts vary
legal_status: No judicial finding in reviewed sources; investigate forcible transfer and treatment of captives under law applicable in 1948
scope_decision: Include capture, detention, and expulsion as separate linked claims; do not treat the contemporary dispatch alone as proof of the full expulsion total
limitations: Contemporary dispatch records prisoners and the town's surrender, but does not itself document the full expulsion. Later record identifies Operation Dani and the expulsion; overall refugee totals for 1948 are not attributed wholesale to Israel here.

event_categories: air and land attacks; forced evacuation; destruction of villages; alleged killings/captures
affected_people_or_estimate: UN observers located more than 4,000 villagers; fewer than 130 were reported killed or missing; separate UN yearbook summary says more than 8,000 located
evidence_summary: UN Mediator cable and UN Yearbook summary based on UN observer investigation
evidence_status: UN investigation confirms attacks by air and land, forced evacuation, destruction of Ein Ghazal and Jaba, and failure to pursue villagers' offer to negotiate; mass-death claims were found exaggerated
legal_status: Mediator stated actions were unjustified and systematic destruction excessive, violating the spirit and letter of the truce; not a criminal judgment
scope_decision: Include UN-confirmed action and UN legal characterization; retain numerical discrepancy between source versions
limitations: Counts differ between the Mediator's cable (>4,000 located) and Yearbook summary (>8,000). Do not collapse or average. UN report says Ijzim's houses were damaged, while Ein Ghazal and Jaba were destroyed.

event_categories: capture; civilian internment; interrogation; forced labor; reported torture, beatings, shootings and deprivation
affected_people_or_estimate: Authors estimate around 5,000 Palestinian civilian internees in four official camps; separate ICRC POW tallies include military prisoners and are not a pure Palestinian-civilian count
evidence_summary: ICRC reports and 1948 field visits, later analyzed in Journal of Palestine Studies; ICRC historical summary confirms visits to Arab POWs in Israel
evidence_status: Multiple former detainee testimonies; ICRC records cited by authors include abuse injuries, beatings and poor conditions; article reports forced labor and civilians held alongside military POWs
legal_status: Potential unlawful civilian internment, forced labor and abuse require legal analysis; no court finding in sources reviewed
scope_decision: Include detainee-treatment allegations and source-linked population estimate; do not present all POW tallies as civilian detainee totals
limitations: The JPS article draws on ICRC archives, survivor interviews and secondary research. Some torture details are survivor testimony; distinguish from direct ICRC observations. 1949 Geneva Convention postdates these events.

event_name: Central Galilee villages (including al-Bi'na and neighboring communities)
event_categories: Operation Hiram; mass displacement; roundup and detention of men and boys
affected_people_or_estimate: An estimated three-quarters of roughly 60,000 Palestinian Arab inhabitants displaced; hundreds of men and boys detained; about 200 men from al-Bi'na reported captured
evidence_summary: Later Journal of Palestine Studies article cites survivor testimony and a 16 November 1948 UN observer report
evidence_status: Article reports displacement during the operation and detention of noncombatant village men; evidence includes named oral testimony and UN observer report
legal_status: No judicial finding in reviewed sources; investigate civilian protection, expulsion, and detention allegations
scope_decision: Include as a documented research case with estimates attributed to the cited author and underlying records
limitations: The 60,000 figure is the estimated Arab population of the area; three-quarters is an estimate, not a household-level displacement count.

event_categories: capture; expulsion to Gaza; detention and forced labor of captive men
affected_people_or_estimate: JPS article cites Ben-Gurion's diary noting around 100 men held captive, put to work, then sent to a prison camp; most of the town population was expelled to Gaza
evidence_summary: Later historical study citing Ben-Gurion's wartime diary and Palestinian detainee sources
evidence_status: Capture and displacement reported by historical sources; detention of about 100 men is tied to Ben-Gurion diary entry
legal_status: No judicial finding in reviewed sources; assess expulsion and treatment separately
scope_decision: Include as a source-linked episode; mark population count and transfer chronology for verification
limitations: Not a direct contemporary news dispatch; cross-check diary entry and refugee records before using a precise total.

actor_as_reported: Israeli forces (occupation acknowledged; alleged killings denied by Israel)
affected_people_or_estimate: No independently verified victim count in sources reviewed
evidence_summary: Arab Refugee Congress allegation recorded by UN Conciliation Commission; Israeli government's 8 November letter denies atrocity and says civilians had left before occupation
evidence_status: Contested allegation; available records include the allegation and formal denial, not a completed independent fact-finding determination
legal_status: No judicial finding in sources reviewed
scope_decision: Keep in allegation queue; do not count fatalities as confirmed until independent corroboration is found
limitations: The UN working paper preserves an Arab Refugee Congress account, while Israel's letter contests the claim and location naming. Seek UN observer notes, British records, and independent contemporaneous reporting.

affected_people_or_estimate: Palestinian Arab civilian population reported fleeing; no count or casualties stated
evidence_summary: Associated Press dispatch dated 19 October says Israeli bombing had entered its fourth day and civilians were reported fleeing; UN observers had left the port city
evidence_status: Contemporaneous foreign press report; flight extent explicitly unknown in the clipping
legal_status: No legal finding; the dispatch alone does not establish target selection, proportionality, or a war crime
scope_decision: Include reported bombing and displacement context; no fatalities or displaced-person total counted
limitations: Partial newspaper clipping; distinguish reported flight from verified displacement and do not infer casualty totals

event_name: Israeli aerial and artillery attacks in Gaza and refugee camps
location: Gaza city; Khan Yunis; Bureij; Rafah; Deir al-Balah
actor_as_reported: Israeli military (attributed by ICRC delegation as reported in peer-reviewed study)
event_categories: air and artillery bombardment; deaths and injuries in civilian/refugee locations
affected_people_or_estimate: About 190 killed and more than 400 wounded across six incidents, as reported by ICRC delegation; source excerpt does not disaggregate civilians and combatants
evidence_summary: Abu Sitta and Rempel report six intensive Israeli aerial and artillery bombing incidents in Gaza city and four refugee camps over six days, citing ICRC field reporting; the delegation head described the attacks as lacking military objectives
evidence_status: Secondary historical study based on ICRC records; strong contemporaneous institutional basis, original archival report not yet reviewed
legal_status: Potential distinction, proportionality, and civilian-protection violations warrant investigation; no criminal court finding identified
scope_decision: Include as a six-day incident series, not six fully documented individual rows; preserve ICRC-attributed totals and obtain original reports
limitations: The published summary gives combined deaths/injuries and omits individual incident breakdown and casualty status; reported no-military-objective characterization is the cited ICRC delegate's assessment

event_name: Capture and continued detention of Palestinian villagers
actor_as_reported: Israeli forces and authorities (UN observers / ICRC, as cited in study)
event_categories: capture; detention without due process; alleged arbitrary detention
affected_people_or_estimate: Two named villagers captured near Tubas in January; broader number not stated
evidence_summary: Peer-reviewed study cites UN truce observers' report that Israeli forces captured Ahmad Abd Abu Zaydi and Yusuf Hamid al-Fustuk while they worked their land near Tubas; it also quotes April ICRC mission head Jacques de Reynier that able-bodied men continued to be arrested and put in camps without due process
evidence_status: Secondary scholarship citing contemporaneous UN and ICRC records; named villagers' later fate not established here
legal_status: Potential arbitrary detention; no court finding in reviewed sources
scope_decision: Include detention pattern and named case lead; do not invent total detainees
limitations: Full UN observer and ICRC April reports not yet retrieved; study presents a broader argument about detention continuing after hostilities

event_name: Israeli settlement and repopulation on depopulated Palestinian land
actor_as_reported: Israeli Government and new Jewish settlers (as reported by New York Times)
event_categories: land takeover; settlement expansion; prevention of return context
affected_people_or_estimate: Nine settlements described as beginning in south after bulldozers cleared a wrecked Arab village; seven more reported started in Galilee; 51 planned
evidence_summary: Anne O'Hare McCormick reported rapid state resettlement on land left by Palestinians and characterized it as parallel to military occupation; she said this made refugee return unlikely
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press account; records reported starts and plans rather than verified completion or legal title for each parcel
legal_status: Territorial/return implications require legal and property-record review; this row records expansion and displacement context, not a judicial legal finding
scope_decision: Include as expansionism evidence and reported state policy; keep settlement counts distinct from completed construction
limitations: NYT's 750000 refugee estimate is a broad conflict total, not an Israeli-attributed 1949 displacement count; land boundaries and individual village names need follow-up

actor_as_reported: Israeli authorities (reported by an expelled resident)
evidence_summary: A short U.S. newspaper brief from Amman attributes the report to a deported Catholic resident who described Israeli authorities' treatment as intolerable
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press report based on single witness account; independently uncorroborated in sources reviewed
legal_status: Potential forcible transfer; no legal finding
scope_decision: Include as a sourced allegation with low confidence pending corroboration; do not merge with annual displacement totals
limitations: Verify the witness identity, date and legal basis of expulsion; do not extrapolate beyond the 41 reported men

event_name: Refugee overcrowding in Egyptian-held southern Palestine
location: Gaza; Khan Yunis; Rafah; Deir al-Balah
actor_as_reported: Context: refugees in Egyptian-held area; not attributed as a discrete Israeli operation
affected_people_or_estimate: Egyptian Army representatives estimated 225000 refugees behind Egyptian lines: 70000 in Gaza and 95000 in Khan Yunis
evidence_summary: Associated Press field report describes crowded former barracks, prison cells, tents and caves, and records the Egyptian Army representatives' population estimates
evidence_status: Contemporaneous foreign press reporting; camp totals attributed to Egyptian Army representatives
legal_status: Not a separate Israeli crime finding and not counted as Israeli-attributed 1949 displacement
scope_decision: Include as humanitarian context only, explicitly outside Israel-attributed incident counts
limitations: Reported population is a stock estimate of refugees present, not a new displacement flow in 1949; AP dispatch reports Egyptian-held geography

event_name: El Auja Bedouin roundup and expulsion
location: El Auja demilitarized zone and Negev; across Egypt border
event_categories: military roundup; forced cross-border expulsion; deaths reported; destruction of tents crops and possessions
affected_people_or_estimate: About 4,000 Bedouins expelled by 2 September; 13 deaths reported in statements collected by the Mixed Armistice Commission investigation
evidence_summary: UNTSO Chief of Staff Riley transmitted the 6 September commission investigation: five tribes' representatives said Israeli operations to clear the area began 20 August, used troops armored cars and reconnaissance aircraft, expelled the group into Egypt, and burned tents crops and possessions; they reported 13 Bedouin killed
evidence_status: UN truce-supervision report documents roundup and expulsion; 13-death figure is testimony relayed by the investigation; Israel denied entering the demilitarized zone and said El Auja residents followed expelled Bedouins, describing the group as infiltrators
legal_status: Potential forcible transfer, civilian-protection and armistice violations warrant investigation; no criminal court finding
scope_decision: Include Israeli military conduct and clearly state the disagreement over zone entry and death attribution
limitations: UN report says approximately 4,000 by 2 September; separate roughly 1,000 Arab expulsions since March are reported in same document and may overlap; do not sum without case-level reconciliation

event_name: Transfer/expulsion of Palestinian Arab residents from Majdal to Gaza
event_categories: expulsion or coerced transfer; displacement; continued settlement/repopulation context
affected_people_or_estimate: UN commission later records about 2,000 Arabs expelled; JTA reports final 75 families transferred by 15 October
evidence_summary: JTA contemporaneously reported completion of the transfer of the last 75 Arab families from Migdal Gad to Gaza; UN Mixed Armistice Commission report in 1951 records about 2,000 Arabs expelled by Israeli authorities and directed repatriation/restoration for those deemed entitled
evidence_status: Contemporary foreign press confirms transfer; subsequent UN commission characterizes it as expulsion; Israeli account and family reunification rationale should be checked against full proceedings
legal_status: Potential forcible transfer and property/restoration issues; UN commission action is not a criminal judgment
scope_decision: Include with contemporaneous and later UN evidence; preserve ambiguity about consent and population scope
limitations: About 2,000 is the commission's case estimate; 75 families is the last group reported, not the total displaced; avoid implying exact date or that all 2,000 were sent in October

event_name: Reported uprooting and land confiscation in Wadi Ara villages
actor_as_reported: Israeli authorities (attribution from historical context; contemporary press claim requires original article review)
event_categories: reported forced displacement; village uprooting; land confiscation
affected_people_or_estimate: Residents of 13 small villages; number of people not stated
evidence_summary: Adel Manna cites the contemporary Palestinian newspaper Al-Ittihad (10 February 1951), which reported that inhabitants of thirteen small villages in Wadi Ara were uprooted and their lands confiscated; a 1984 UN Special Committee report likewise records the expulsion and confiscation
evidence_status: Contemporary Palestinian press report accessed through peer-reviewed historical scholarship, with later UN corroboration; original Arabic article not yet reviewed
legal_status: Potential forcible transfer and property seizure; no criminal judgment identified
scope_decision: Include as a documented lead with population count unknown; verify village names and individual orders before annual totals
limitations: Do not estimate displaced persons from village count; later UN report's framing and underlying sources need review; attribution to Israeli authorities is contextual pending direct text

event_name: Jordanian complaints of Israeli-force attacks on border villages
location: Beit Iksa; Beit Surik; Yalu; Saffa; Sharafat; Falam; Deir Ballut; Imwas
actor_as_reported: Israeli armed forces (as alleged in complaints listed by UNTSO)
event_categories: reported village attacks; shootings; civilian deaths; home destruction
affected_people_or_estimate: Jordanian complaints listed two civilians killed in Saffa, ten killed and eight wounded in Sharafat, and one man and two children killed in Falam; other complaints give no casualty count
evidence_summary: UNTSO report S/2048 lists Jordanian complaints alleging Israeli-force attacks on multiple villages between late January and mid-February. The Mixed Armistice Commission later condemned wanton killings and home destruction collectively, but said the complaints had been acted upon without adjudicating each listed claim separately
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN record of complaints and a collective commission response; individual allegations not separately verified in the cited report
legal_status: Potential unlawful attacks and killings; commission resolution is armistice oversight, not a criminal judgment
scope_decision: Include only alleged Israeli actions; do not record Arab-party complaints as incidents or sum reported deaths as a confirmed toll
limitations: Jordanian complaint figures; no event-level investigation results given in this section; preserve reported versus confirmed status and avoid treating the 23 fatality claims as verified aggregate

event_categories: artillery or mortar shelling; truce violation
affected_people_or_estimate: No casualty number in the cited Commission finding
evidence_summary: The Jordan-Israel Mixed Armistice Commission found shelling by Israeli forces constituted a technical violation of the General Armistice Agreement and condemned it; the same decision stated the violation resulted from lesser contraventions by Jordanian residents
evidence_status: Contemporaneous UN armistice finding; precise weapon and casualties are not established in the quoted decision
legal_status: Formal armistice violation finding; not a criminal court determination
scope_decision: Include the Israeli force action and preserve the Commission's causal/context qualification
limitations: The Commission said demarcation lines were not clearly marked and ordered ground marking and local telephone links; no casualty tally supplied
